label: prf:skein-bar-antisymmetry
title: Proof of skein bar antisymmetry
html:
Proof. Proof of skein bar antisymmetry

Proof. The bar involution swaps L_+ \leftrightarrow L_- and q \leftrightarrow q^{-1} while fixing L_0. Direct substitution gives both equalities above. \square

Corollary (case-split collapse).

Any proof in the braid--knot framework that establishes a property \Phi(L_+) for the positive crossing automatically establishes \Phi(L_-) for the negative crossing, provided \Phi is formulated \overline{\,\cdot\,}-equivariantly (i.e., \Phi(\overline{x}) = \overline{\Phi(x)} on the relevant target). The bar involution transports the proof verbatim.

Wherever the corollary applies — a pair of positive/negative crossing computations, a per-crossing-sign feasibility check, an enumeration of L_+ and L_- contributions to a state sum — the bar-antisymmetry of (S) means those contributions enter the analysis as bar-paired terms, not independent ones. The case-split is pure bookkeeping.

Connection to substrate bar T-duality.

Bar-antisymmetry of (S) is the algebraic origin of the substrate-level bar T-duality (bar T-duality substrate): the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M \colon H_n(q) \to \mathbb{C}(q) commutes with \overline{\,\cdot\,} up to sign on antisymmetric elements, so the geometric bar-pairing on the moduli of \mathcal{E}_q inherits its sign structure from (S).

Categorical statement.

The bar involution defines a contravariant functor \overline{\,\cdot\,} \colon H_n(q) \to H_n(q^{-1})^{\mathrm{op}} sending each generator \sigma_i to \sigma_i^{-1} in the opposite algebra. The Skein relation is the assertion that this functor intertwines the two crossing types, with the sign flip in (S) encoding the antisymmetry.
